content: I seem to have missed the same step as others have described. But I used that 2mm key tip from HappyKatz. I also noticed that the 3rd fasterner that does not get disturbed seems to keep the belt tensioner in place (with the 2mm key also used).

Same as the other commenters, there's definitely a step missing because I still had screws in place in the belt tensioner. I removed the fan did the following:
1. Release the belt tension (counting turns)
2. Remove the screws from the belt tensioner
3. Connect the dock fan cable and then install the dock fan (this allows the use of the regular side of the allen key and doesn't require putting a screw in 1/4 turn at a time!)
4. THEN install the fan and connect it
5. Re-tighten the belt tensioner the same number of turns it had been loosened.

They forgot the stop where you have to remove the two existing screws. If there is tension on the belts, the bracket will probably shift and you'll have to push it back into place to match up the holes. I removed the fan temporarily so I could just access the front screw with a regular hex screwdriver.
is there a step missing to remove the two existing screws out of the tensioner to replace with the longer ones installed into the fan ?

replies.content: Same. I cannot find any step that calls for removing the two tensioner screws.

content:
2mm hex key is the MVP of this assembly so far and scores points here, too. 

Your belts are probably under sufficient tension to move the belt tensioner slightly out of alignment with respect to the holes. Moving the small hex key through the hole in the belt tensioner and the frame will show you how to counter the tension with your thumb and hold the belt tensioner in its proper place long enough to secure the first front fan mount screw.
